title: Training
core_thesis: Physical AI policy training must reconcile the sample efficiency and safety of offline or simulated optimization with the unyielding reality of unmodeled hardware dynamics and compounding out-of-distribution execution errors.
pedagogical_strengths: Grounds abstract machine learning failure modes (like L2 mode averaging) in tangible physical consequences, such as destructive maneuvers or gear wear.
Clearly frames the sim-to-real gap as 'modeling debt' that gradient descent naturally and aggressively exploits.

student_friction_points.point: The acronym 'ACT' is introduced alongside Diffusion and Flow Matching without prior expansion or grounding, disrupting cognitive flow for readers unfamiliar with recent imitation learning architectures.
The introduction of Action Chunking lacks an immediate bridge to classical control theory; students may wonder how this predictive horizon relates to Model Predictive Control (MPC).

established_budgets_and_laws: Quadratic compounding error bounds (O(T^2 epsilon)) for single-step behavioral cloning policies.
Hardware and thermal budgets as hard constraints against unphysical high-frequency torque chatter.
imported_prerequisites: Actuator thermal limits and duty cycles (@sec-body-thermal-duty-cycles)
Rigid body dynamics and actuator limits (@sec-body-actuator-limits)
exported_concepts: Sim-to-real modeling debt and domain randomization limits
Compounding covariate shift in closed-loop physical execution
Action chunking as a defense against high-frequency mode chatter

surgical_edits.target_text: Action Chunking in Diffusion, Flow Matching, and ACT defends against quadratic compounding error ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$).
surgical_edits.improved_text: Action chunking—predicting a temporal sequence of future commands rather than a single instantaneous action—defends against quadratic compounding error ($\mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon)$). It serves as a core stabilization mechanism in recent generative architectures, including diffusion models and Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT).

surgical_edits.target_text: The same commands can produce vibration or failure
surgical_edits.improved_text: Deployed on physical hardware, these identical commands often trigger destructive high-frequency vibrations or outright mechanical failure.

open_thematic_threads_for_part: How do we systematically benchmark, bound, and evaluate policies that carry unmodeled simulation debt before granting them full operational authority on physical hardware?
